items.note: Read CVDR754219/1 in full. Council session 18 Dec 2025 (signature), in force 1 Jan 2026 (art. 12). Tarieventabel art. 1.1a for Sneek streets and lots (excluding the two garages): 1,03 per half hour up to two hours, 1,54 per half hour from two hours; first half hour per day 0,00 if the plate is registered via the machine or directly after start in the central computer. All numbers and conditions match.

Same page, Tarieventabel art. 1.1b: garages Zuid Waterpoort and Oost Normandiaplein first 24 hours free, after 24 hours 1,54 per half hour, maximum 5,00 per day; art. 1.2 says garage tariffs include VAT. The page uses the short names without 'P-' and does not mention the former name Boschplein; that is in the Aanwijzingsbesluit (item 3), so the renaming remark is supported elsewhere.

Read CVDR732023/1 (2025 ordinance, council 19 Dec 2024, valid 1 Jan to 31 Dec 2025). 2025 table for Sneek streets/lots: first half hour per day free (no registration condition), 1,00 per half hour up to two hours, 1,50 from two hours; garages first 24 h free, then 1,50 per half hour, max 5,00. The garage per-half-hour rate rose from 1,50 to 1,54, but the item only claims the 24-hour free period and the 5,00 daily maximum were unchanged, which is correct. Date 2025-01 is the in-force month; council decision was 19 Dec 2024.

Read CVDR734311/1. Decided by the college on 7 Jan 2025, valid from 16-01-2025 'met terugwerkende kracht vanaf 01-01-2025'. Art. 1: Sneek Mon-Sat 9.00-21.00, Sun 13.00-21.00 (public holidays and 31 Dec treated as Sunday); garages 0.00-24.00. Considerations record the March 2024 renames (Boschpleingarage to P-Zuid Waterpoort, Normandiagarage to P-Oost Normandiaplein, Veemarkt to P-West Theater, Bolswarderpoort to P-Noord Bolswarderpoort). Note: this is the 2025 designation and the page still shows it as valid 't/m heden' on 21 Oct 2026; I found no 2026 designation in the national repository (SRU search of Sudwest-Fryslan parkeerbelastingen titles), but the 2026 ordinance art. 8 leaves designation to the college, so current hours rest on the 2025 decision.

Same page, art. 2 lists items a to ff = exactly 32 Sneek streets and lots (surface and one deck), plus art. 2.3 lists the two garages separately. Named examples all present: Boschplein (maaiveld), Normandiaplein (maaiveld), Sint Antoniusplein (maaiveld) and Parkeerdek, Lemmerweg, Leeuwarderweg, Martiniplein, Oude Koemarkt, Parkeerterrein Steenklip, P-Noord Bolswarderpoort (westelijk deel), P-West Theater (noordwestelijk deel). Art. 4: payment by bank card or by phone login with a provider linked to SHPV. 'About 32' is exact (32).

CVDR754219/1 Tarieventabel art. 2: resident permit inside the canals 106,00 per year; business permit inside and outside canals (short stay) 495,00 per year; permit outside the canals (lang parkeren) 30,00 per month or 300,00 per year. All equal to the 2025 table (CVDR732023/1). But the 2026 page does not say that the long-stay permit covers 'the garages'; that link is only inferable from the 2021 Nadere regels (item 6), so the parenthetical is not supported by this source.
items.corrected_text: Resident permits for paid zones inside the Sneek canals cost 106.00 euros per year in 2026, business permits (short stay, inside and outside the canals) 495.00 euros per year, and permits for long-stay parking outside the canals 30.00 euros per month or 300.00 euros per year. These permit prices are identical to those in the 2025 table.

items.note: Read CVDR655435. Decided by the college 23 Feb 2021, in force 1 March 2021, shown as valid 't/m heden'. Art. 9.1: for areas 1.1 and 1.2 at most 2 permits per address (residents of 1.1 qualify for only one if they have own parking). Art. 11: subscriptions (category 3) are for area 1.2 only and holders can ask for a pass to enter/leave the Boschplein and Normandia garages. Not on the page: that 1.1 means 'inside and outside the canals', that 1.2 is 'long stay outside the canals including the garages' (the areas are defined in a separate Aanwijzingsbesluit 2020-2, not read), the word Sneek, and '13 resident zones' (the page only refers to areas 2.1 to 2.13/2.20 across the municipality, including Bolsward). The 'residents of area 1.1 get at most two permits' claim is correct but incomplete.
items.corrected_text: The municipality's permit rules (Nadere regels parkeervergunningen en -ontheffingen 2021, decided by the executive on 23 February 2021, in force from 1 March 2021 and still shown as in force) allow at most two permits per address for resident areas 1.1 and 1.2, and only one if the resident has own parking. Subscription permits (category 3) are valid only for area 1.2, and their holders can request a pass to enter and leave the Boschplein and Normandia garages (old names). Permits for areas 1.1 and 1.2 are valid Monday to Saturday 09:00-21:00. The geographic definition of the areas is in a separate designation decision that was not read.

items.note: Read gmb-2023-297788. Published and signed 11 July 2023 by the college. Doorrijverbod by signs and enforcement cameras, no physical closure, on Singel, Prins Hendrikkade, Harinxmakade and Kleine Kerkstraat; Prins Hendrikkade, Singel and Harinxmakade 12.00-18.00 seven days a week, but Kleine Kerkstraat 12.00-07.00 seven days a week (existing closure, hours aligned with hospitality). The item says all four routes are 12:00-18:00, which is wrong for Kleine Kerkstraat. Parking statements (homes, businesses and parking places stay reachable; large car parks/transfer points within walking distance; enough spaces in the centre for quick errands and visitors with reduced mobility) match. Page also says the trial was planned 2 Oct 2023 to 30 Sep 2024 (actual start 2 Jan 2024 per item 8). Also a trial truck ban on Harinxmakade 12-18 h.
items.corrected_text: On 11 July 2023 the executive of Súdwest-Fryslân decided a trial 'autoluwe binnenstad' for Sneek: no physical closure, but signs and enforcement cameras on four through-routes. Through traffic was to be banned on Singel, Prins Hendrikkade and Harinxmakade from 12:00 to 18:00 seven days a week, and on Kleine Kerkstraat from 12:00 to 07:00 seven days a week (an existing closure); buses and (moped) cyclists were exempt on the first three. The decision states that all homes, businesses and parking places in the centre stay reachable and that the parking policy places the large car parks (transfer points) within walking distance of the centre, with enough spaces in the centre for quick errands and for visitors with reduced mobility.

items.note: Read gmb-2024-101874 (Gemeenteblad published 6 March 2024, signed 'Sneek, 4 maart 2024'; the October 2024 decision itself cites it as 'besluit van 6 maart 2024'). Trial started 2 Jan 2024; after the first monitoring round the end time of the bans on Prins Hendrikkade, Singel and Harinxmakade was cut from 18:00 to 17:00; traffic per day on Prins Hendrikkade and Singel down 37-49 percent against a target of at least 25 percent; traffic pressure on Worp Tjaardastraat/Goeman Borgesiuslaan/Berkenlaan and Willem Lodewijkstraat strongly increased in peak periods. The decision takes effect six weeks after publication. All claims match.

Read gmb-2024-433843 (published 17 Oct 2024, signed 15 Oct 2024). Withdrawal of the Prins Hendrikkade ban confirmed; ban had been out of the trial temporarily since 19 June 2024 for four months; reasons: much incomprehension, street used mainly as traffic space; counts Sept 2023 about 9,000 per day (Prins Hendrikkade) and 6,000 (Singel), about halved in January 2024. Not on the page: that the bans on the other routes 'continued as part of the trial'. The decision only amends the Prins Hendrikkade part, and the text says the other bans are better understood, but it gives no statement about their continuation or the trial's end (originally planned to end 30 Sep 2024).
items.corrected_text: On 15 October 2024 the executive withdrew the through-traffic ban on Prins Hendrikkade (it had been taken out of the trial temporarily since 19 June 2024), citing much public incomprehension and that the street is used mainly as traffic space rather than as a place to stay; counts of September 2023 gave about 9,000 vehicles per day on Prins Hendrikkade and 6,000 on Singel, roughly halved in January 2024. The decision amends only the Prins Hendrikkade ban; the decision text notes the other bans are better understood.

items.note: Read gmb-2022-144068 (published 31 March 2022). Decision designates two parking places per charge point as charging-only at five locations: Wassenberghstraat 18 (Sneek), Reafinne 18 (Oudega), De Hoppen 1 (Sneek), Kleine Vos 32 (Sneek), De Skarren 28 (Bolsward); only one bay per location is actually equipped now, second added if demand arises. The page does not call the locations 'residential' or 'neighbourhood', and two of the five are outside Sneek; the 'not the town-centre car parks' remark is the researcher's inference (the decision gives only addresses).
items.corrected_text: A collective traffic decision published on 31 March 2022 designates two parking places per charge point as charging-only bays at five locations (Wassenberghstraat 18, De Hoppen 1 and Kleine Vos 32 in Sneek, Reafinne 18 in Oudega and De Skarren 28 in Bolsward), but only one bay per location is actually equipped initially, with the second to be added if demand shows.

items.note: Read gmb-2026-363823.pdf (60 pages, all read). Decision text: adopted by the college in its meeting of 10 February 2026; Gemeenteblad 2026 nr. 363823 dated 28 July 2026; programme title 'Samen vooruit naar 2040'. Para 8.3.5 'Auto te gast': in Bolsward and Sneek to lead through traffic 'zoveel mogelijk' around the centre; cars are guests in these inner cities. Wording as an aim is accurate (item says 'aims to'); the Sneekweek decision (item 15) independently confirms 10 Feb 2026.

Same PDF. Para 8.3.6 and p. 29 confirm: transferpunten are large car parks where roads from outside end and from which visitors walk or use public transport; Sneek already has several, a short walk from the inner city and with shops for daily groceries; new ones at strategic spots well connected to public transport. Para 8.3.8: the programme says it wants to align ('aansluiten') with the Parkeervisie (2019) and a Parkeernormennota (which determines how many parking places new developments need); for urban areas the ultimate goal is to investigate where combinations and built parking are possible. The item says 'Sneek's parking follows the Parkeervisie of 2019', which is stronger than the page: it is a municipality-wide vision the programme intends to connect to, and Sneek is not named there.
items.corrected_text: The Mobiliteitsprogramma describes 'transferpunten' as large car parks where roads from outside end and visitors walk or use public transport; it says Sneek already has several, within short walking distance of the inner city and near shops for daily groceries, and that new ones are to be placed at strategic spots well connected to public transport. On parking it says it wants to align with the municipality's Parkeervisie (2019) and a Parkeernormennota (which sets how many parking places new developments need), and that in urban areas the ultimate aim is to investigate where combined and built (structured) parking is possible.

items.note: Same PDF. p. 29: 'Verkenning inzetten station Sneek als multifunctionele hub incl. Blue Mobility en TOP-locatie' and 'Onderzoeken, upgraden en/of realiseren mobiliteitshubs en transferpunten (o.a. ... Oppenhuizerweg Sneek)' listed under 'Wat nemen we mee in het Uitvoeringsprogramma'; 'zoekgebied aan de Oppenhuizerweg in Sneek'; para 9.4: Blue Mobility 'kan een schakel vormen' to move people from the Sneek transfer points to the inner city. Exploration status is stated correctly (programme says the implementation programme has yet to be drawn up).

Same PDF. Para 8.3.7: municipality applies a charging policy ('laadbeleid') for an adequate public charging network, links to mobility hubs possible; implementation programme lists 'Uitbreiden laadnetwerk' and 'Inzetten op toereikende laadinfra (koppeling met mobiliteitshubs)'. I searched the whole text for 'laad' and found no charger numbers for Sneek.

Read gmb-2026-306011 (published 26 June 2026). Confirmed: centre closed to motor traffic 31 July to 6 August 2026, 19:00-02:30 (from Parkstraat, Leeuwarderweg, Oppenhuizerweg, Singel, Prins Hendrikkade, Looxmagracht/Koninginnebrug, Lemmerweg); Martiniplein 28 July to 6 August 08:00-19:00 full closure to through traffic (pedestrian area, sign G7). The attached image exb-2026-22522 (a map) shows P-Noord Bolswarderpoort (Bolswarderweg 11), P-Station Sneek (Kanaalstraat 24), P-West Theater (Korte Veemarktstraat 12), P-Zuid Waterpoort (Boschplein 7), P-Oost Normandiaplein (Normandiaplein 7) and Zuidersportpark, plus unnamed P symbols. Not supported: 'event 31 July to 7 August' (the decision says the Sneekweek starts on the Friday before the first Saturday of August; no end date; Botniakade closure 7 Aug is for dismantling) and 'municipal' parking sites (the map does not say who operates them and the title 'Parkeren rond om Sneek' is only the attachment's link label); also the Martiniplein closure is 08:00-19:00 daily, not continuous.
items.corrected_text: A traffic decision published on 26 June 2026 for the Sneekweek (starting on the Friday before the first Saturday of August, i.e. 31 July 2026; set-up and dismantling around it) closes the centre of Sneek to motor traffic from 19:00 to 02:30 from 31 July to 6 August 2026, and closes the Martiniplein to through traffic from 08:00 to 19:00 on 28 July to 6 August (pedestrian area). The attached map 'Parkeren rond om Sneek' marks the parking sites P-Noord Bolswarderpoort, P-Station Sneek (Kanaalstraat 24), P-West Theater (Korte Veemarktstraat 12), P-Zuid Waterpoort (Boschplein 7), P-Oost Normandiaplein (Normandiaplein 7) and the Zuidersportpark; the map does not say who operates them.

items.note: Read gmb-2026-52628.pdf (102 pages, all read). Council decision 29 January 2026, Gemeenteblad 4 February 2026; the decision amends the Omgevingsvisie (mainly the Wonen part). Sneek 2050 section (p. 80): 'parkeren op maaiveld in de centrumzone niet meer gewenst, dit wordt uitgefaseerd. Verkennen waar parkeren wel kan, in gebouwde parkeerhubs aan de rand van de centrumzone'; 'Meer woningen en voorzieningen mag niet leiden tot meer auto's in de binnenstad.' It is a 2050 vision with no construction programme, as the item says.

Same PDF. Area table (p. 81): Spoorzone/Veemarktterrein 'mogelijkheden onderzoeken om ruimte te creëren voor groen verblijfs- en evenementengebied ... door bijvoorbeeld gebouwde alternatieven voor maaiveldparkeren' and 'Onderzoek naar de wegen-, parkeer-, ov- en langzaam verkeersstructuur'; 'multifunctionele en multimodale stationshub'; building category 5: up to 10 layers at the station area (Spoorzone). All presented as explorations, matching the item.

Fetched the page with curl on 21 Oct 2026 (HTTP 200). Q-Park P+R Station, Sneek, Kanaalstraat, 8601 GA Sneek; Parkeerplaatsen 126; Doorrijhoogte 1.90 m; opening Monday-Sunday arrival 24-7, departure 24-7; traveller discount conditions as stated; tariffs 'konden helaas niet geladen worden'. The Q-Park Sneek city page lists exactly 1 facility, so 'only Sneek facility' is supported. Live, undated page; the item correctly says it was read on 21 October 2026. Caveat: the Sneekweek map (item 15) lists a 'P-Station Sneek' at Kanaalstraat 24; whether that is the same site as Q-Park's P+R is not established.

corrected_summary: Sneek's paid parking is a municipal regime set by Súdwest-Fryslân. Under the 2025 designation decision (still shown as in force on 21 October 2026) street and surface parking is paid Monday to Saturday 09:00-21:00 and Sunday 13:00-21:00 (public holidays as Sunday), and the two garages P-Zuid Waterpoort (formerly Boschplein) and P-Oost Normandiaplein are paid round the clock; the designation lists 32 paid streets and lots. The Verordening Parkeerbelastingen 2026 (council decision of 18 December 2025, in force 1 January 2026) charges 1.03 euros per half hour up to two hours and 1.54 euros per half hour beyond, with the first half hour per day free only if the licence plate is registered (in 2025 the first half hour was free unconditionally and the rates were 1.00 and 1.50 euros). In the two garages the first 24 hours are free, then 1.54 euros per half hour up to 5.00 euros per day, including VAT. Resident permits inside the canals cost 106 euros per year, unchanged from 2025. Policy is moving towards fewer cars in the centre: a trial 'autoluwe binnenstad' with camera-enforced through-traffic bans started in January 2024 (traffic on Prins Hendrikkade and Singel fell 37-49 percent in the first monitoring round; the Prins Hendrikkade ban was withdrawn in October 2024); the Omgevingsvisie amended by the council on 29 January 2026 states a long-term vision (to 2050) of phasing out surface parking in the centre zone in favour of built parking hubs at its edge, with only explorations for the station and Veemarkt area; and the Mobiliteitsprogramma adopted by the executive on 10 February 2026 (published 28 July 2026) aims to lead through traffic around the centre, to keep and add 'transferpunten' at the edge of the centre, and lists explorations of a station hub and a search area on Oppenhuizerweg. The station P+R at Kanaalstraat is a Q-Park site with 126 spaces, open 24/7 (page read on 21 October 2026, tariff not shown). The outcome of the trial's evaluation, later council decisions, the Parkeervisie 2019 and any utilisation or occupancy figures could not be read, because the municipality's website was offline (HTTP 503 on two attempts) and the council information systems block automated access.
